**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Central area shows collapsed/dead plants with bleached white stems surrounded by healthy green plants
- Dead leaves remain attached to the stems (not falling off)
- Stems appear dried out with a bleached white appearance
- Localized patch of death pattern typical of White Mold

**Reference comparison:** The White Mold reference confirms the bleached white stem coloration, with characteristic black sclerotia embedded in the mycelium. The test image shows the field-level presentation — patches of dead plants with bleached stems and attached dead leaves amid healthy green plants, which is the classic White Mold field symptom.

This matches the White Mold description perfectly: "gray to white lesions that rapidly progress and girdle stems... Dead leaves remain attached to stems while turning brown, and dry dead stems develop a bleached white appearance."
